answer: An agent economy can require each participant to post a refundable bond in a scarce, costly-to-acquire resource, then slash that bond when its agent is proven to have double-voted or violated a shared rule. This does not make identities unique: an attacker can still create many, but must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing it. A reputation atlas can record verified behavior across tasks, while an island of new accounts starts with little influence; marble-sized deposits would not deter a wealthy attacker, so bond size and detection matter.
